additional_info.subject: RE: ID0469965-DC/Si-D/SA-[Y2 / R4 312922184005] OCPP Communication Issue CRM:03042000335
additional_info.body:
Good evening Mohamed,
I am following up our conversation from today in regards of ticket
ID0469965
and charger
Y2/R4 312922184005
for End Customer SASCO.
As mentioned this morning, I see two different problems in the connectivity to the Backend:
The customer router XF4 has issues on the password and is not connected to the mobile network.
This problem is independent form the OCPP Backend, and it is a pure matter of connectivity of the router itself which can be solved.
The customer's OCPP Backend, which as I understood is this "
SASCO-EV-Management
", is a Backend not integrated with Sicharge D, hence we cannot guarantee that the communication between Charger and Backend works without a proper integration.
For the second point, I explained you a possible way forward, with a paid integration activity that con be organized together with the CPO, to ensure that our SichargeD and the customer's OCPP Backend work together according to OCPP 1.6. On this point, I will get back to you at the beginning of next week, once I will align internally with my colleague from the Integration Team.
For the first point, I already remotely checked the charger and the router, and:
The password of the router was the default password of Teltonika RUT240 "admin01". I changed the password and set the charger's password to the router. Now the charger can access the router.
After changing the password, the router managed to connect also with the SIM card to internet:
The main WAN of the router is set to WIRED. Also this connection is working, and it has access to internet:
Can you please confirm that the main connection of the router is voluntarily set to wired, or should it be mobile?
Therefore, the router has internet connection and it is ready to connect to the Backend. I believe at this point what is not working are the settings and information to connect to the Backend. Could you please verify that:
The websocket provided by the end customer is correct
The OCPP ID of the charger inside the Backend is correct
The OCPP ID of the charger is registered inside the Backend
The Backend does not require an OCPP Authorization Key to be set into the charger. At the moment it is not set.
These are the basic requirements for the charger to connect to an OCPP Backend connection. The rest, in case of problems, can be discussed in an integration activity. I will get back to you on this topic next week.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0469965-DC/Si-D/SA-[Y2 / R4 312922184005] OCPP Communication Issue CRM:03042000335
additional_info.body:
Dear Mohamed,
Today I had time to check again the connection to a Backend for charger Y2 / R4 312922184005. Yesterday, during the call with the end customer, we tried to connect the charger to our DepotFinity Backend, but unsuccessfully. Today I checked again and the connection was not possible due to a wrong OCPP Authorization key I was using yesterday, and did not notice while calling.
These are my findings of the day:
I connected to the charger and verified that the mobile connection was in place.
In SCB, I configured the OCPP connection to be connected to our DepotFinity Backend. The charger immediately connected to the Backend:
I then configured the OCPP connection on SCB according to the OCPPChargePointId and URL provided by the end customer:
OCPP ChargePoint ID: SASCO-001
OCPP url:
wss://ocpp-dev.sasco.com.sa:9999/ocpp
After configuring it, I finally saw an error message that was overseen yesterday:
2026-01-27T09:36:23.913923+00:00 [FW060103G1] sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/811b79c221f8[636]: Uncaught Exception: {"stack":"Error: OCPP-Central-System
wss://ocpp-dev.sasco.com.sa:9999/ocpp doesn't support OCPP protocol ocpp1.6\n at WebSocket.
<anonymous> (/node_modules/@sicharge-cp/ocpp-lib/dist/ChargePoint.js:93:35)\n at WebSocket.emit (node:events:518:28)\n at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/node_modules/@sicharge-cp/ocpp-lib/node_modules/ws/lib/websocket.js:589:15)\n at ClientRequest.emit (node:events:518:28)\n at TLSSocket.socketOnData (node:_http_client:584:11)\n at TLSSocket.emit (node:events:518:28)\n at addChunk (node:internal/streams/readable:561:12)\n at readableAddChunkPushByteMode (node:internal/streams/readable:512:3)\n at Readable.push (node:internal/streams/readable:392:5)\n at TLSWrap.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:191:23)"}
It seems that the Backend uses a websocket which does not support OCPP 1.6J protocol.
Therefore, let me resume the way forward:
It is now confirmed that the issue is with the websocket provided by the customer. The customer has to provide a websocket based on OCPP 1.6 protocol. Our charger does not support OCPP 2.0 yet, for example.
This has to be resolved from the Backend side
Once the issue is solved, we can re-configure the OCPP connection via SCB and verify if the charger finally connects to the Backend.
After this, if the customer still requires support for the handling of OCPP messages and functionalities, an OCPP integration paid service has to be ordered, as thoroughly discussed yesterday.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
eMobility Customer Service
Technical Support Engineer

13629 Berlin, Germany
